lesson_title: Four Letters That Run a Business
hook_text: A supermarket launches home deliveries and misses its target by eighty. Here is what a good manager does next.
clip_script: P: plan. Four hundred deliveries a month, thirty-five rand each. Costs are twelve thousand six hundred, so three hundred and sixty just to break even. O: organise. A van, a driver, two packers, an order phone, a supervisor in charge. L: lead. Clear cut-off times, every bag checked, and thank the team when customers say thanks. C: control. Month one: three hundred and twenty deliveries. Eighty percent. Fees eleven thousand two hundred, short by one thousand four hundred. Why? Nobody knew about it, and the phone rang unanswered. Fix: advertise, staff the phone. Month three: four hundred and fifty deliveries, three thousand one hundred and fifty rand to spare. Then back to P.
visual_style: A whiteboard circle divided into P, O, L and C, a delivery van driving around it, a target gauge needle rising from eighty percent to above one hundred.
mood: Upbeat and practical, problem then solution.
pacing: Four quick letter beats, a pause on the missed target, then a satisfying recovery.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run the control cycle yourself.
